reasons: The source says LLM-referred shoppers expect a continuation of the guided conversation and that generic experiences or requiring them to redo the LLM's work lowers conversion probability.

The source's on-site expectation explicitly calls for immediate confirmation of why the merchant matches the shopper's exact brief. The candidate correctly scopes this to visitors arriving after an LLM has performed research, filtering, and buying-coach work.
The core conditional guidance is supported: multivariate tests are trustworthy only above an unspecified traffic-and-variable-count threshold, with sequential A/B tests safer below it.

The prerequisite limits the entire unit to cases above the threshold, while its action also directs what to do below the threshold. This makes the fallback direction inapplicable under the unit's own prerequisites; represent the two branches without making the above-threshold condition a prerequisite for both.

The asserted alternative_to relationship with c7 is not supported by the source. The excerpt presents sequential A/B testing as the safer fallback to multivariate testing below the threshold; it does not present multivariate testing as an alternative to the general valid-A/B-test requirements represented by c7.
The strategic-priorities section explicitly directs readers to test relentlessly and states that a disciplined testing program with a 60%+ win rate generates compounding returns.
The candidate appropriately preserves uncertainty about the measurement period and operational definition of the win-rate figure.
The source identifies forced account creation as a pitfall and states that 62% of sites do not make guest checkout prominent enough.
Making guest checkout prominent is a direct corrective action consistent with the stated pitfall; the candidate does not invent a placement or prominence threshold.
The source explicitly identifies desktop-first mobile design as a pitfall and names tiny thumbnails, unreadable text, and hidden filters as its consequences.
The warning does not add unsupported mobile redesign requirements or numerical thresholds.

The summary explicitly describes a sustained CRO program of testing weekly, documenting learnings, and rolling out wins as the path to compounding profitable growth without proportional ad-spend increases.
The candidate retains the source's three program components and does not add unsupported implementation details.

omissions.description: For the AI-referral experience, provide a curated explanation together with a limited set of recommended options; immediate match confirmation alone does not represent this distinct landing-experience guidance.
Avoid slow mobile pages; the source separately gives a claimed conversion impact for each additional 100 ms, which is not represented by the general LCP/INP recommendation.
omissions.quote: Slow mobile pages — every 100ms costs 3.5% conversion

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-table, so the heading and preceding context for the pre-click versus on-site experience comparison are absent.
The traffic and variable-count threshold for trustworthy multivariate testing is not specified.

The excerpt supplies performance percentages and case-study outcomes without study methods, sample sizes, attribution methods, or linked citations, so their generalizability cannot be assessed from this excerpt.
The excerpt does not define operational measurement rules for concepts such as win rate, sufficient sample size, statistical significance, or revenue per session.
